summary: @servicetitan/examples preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `scripts.preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which auto-executes on `npm install`. setup.mjs is heavily hex-obfuscated (`_0x...` identifiers, string-array indirection) and, when no local `bun` binary is present, downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmod +x's the binary, and invokes it against the shipped `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~730 KB opaque payload marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with a shuffled string/opcode array (`n7gIxM=[...]`, `WV8StW` rotator, `hc1jfK9` decoder) and mangled identifiers, built to be run by the fetched Bun runtime rather than by Node — evading Node-oriented static analysis. The package name `@servicetitan/examples` is inconsistent with a legitimate first-party ServiceTitan publication: description is empty, the dependency list references many `@servicetitan/*` sub-packages as a cover, and the only real install-time effect is executing the obfuscated payload under a freshly-fetched alien runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
